newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended slightly up on Wednesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but profit-taking pushed prices from their intraday highs, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,810 yuan ($2,871) per tonne, up 30 yuan. It opened at 24,000 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 24,010 and a low of 23,800.
June rose 10 to 23,390, July gained 10 to 23,550, August fell 30 to 23,650, October rose 50 to 23,850 and November closed unchanged at 23,840 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume tonnes rose to 51,220 tonnes from 34,700.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking pushed prices down for most of the session, traders said.
Traders said LME gains boosted the confidence of long position holders to some extent but copper met strong resistance at 24,000 yuan.
LME copper hit one-year highs on Tuesday of around $2,500 per tonne in late London inter-office trading. Last kerb business had been at $2,493, up $19 on the day.
"Despite overnight gains on the LME, many investors preferred to stay on the sidelines with copper unable to breach the key resistance level," one Shanghai trader said.
"A large amount of hedging and speculative selling emerged on the market today, preventing copper from rising further," he said.
Physical prices are around 23,350 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, traders said.
Traders said domestic copper producers would rather build short positions above the 24,000-yuan level as production costs are below 20,000 yuan per tonne.
Traders said copper was likely to continue to test 24,000 yuan in the next few days due to the strong upward trend on the LME.
LME copper was seen extending Tuesday's gains, testing higher levels at $2,520 and $2,540 in the near term.
Aluminium ended mixed. June fell 30 to 15,420, July rose 70 to 15,670 and August fell 10 to 15,790 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 570 tonnes from 1,890 tonnes.
